research_problem: No automated tool generated stateful request sequences from a REST API specification to test cloud services
technical_approach: Swagger-derived fuzzing grammar; producer-consumer dependency inference; dynamic-feedback pruning (keep only 2xx sequences); BFS, BFS-Fast, RandomWalk search; small value dictionaries; 500 = bug; GC, token refresh, annotations for production
primary_contribution: RESTler, first stateful REST API fuzzer; evidence that dependencies + feedback are both necessary
dataset_benchmark: 189-LOC blog-posts service with planted bug; GitLab (376K LOC Ruby, 6 API groups); 3 Azure + 1 Office365 services (undisclosed)
evaluation_metrics: Code coverage (Ruby TracePoint), HTTP status distribution, tests/sequence counts, bug buckets
baselines: Own ablations (no dependencies; no feedback) and three search strategies; no external tools
key_findings: Both techniques needed (same coverage with <800 tests in 179s vs 4,600 tests in 1,750s; planted bug found only with dependencies); longer sequences raise coverage; RandomWalk found most bugs (21) despite lower coverage; 28 confirmed/fixed GitLab bugs; bugs in all cloud services tested
author_limitations: No redirect support; oracle limited to status codes (misses e.g. information exposure); generality unknown; RandomWalk results may not generalize
analyst_limitations: Q1 on toy service with self-planted bug; no external baselines; single runs, no statistics; tiny dictionaries; production results undisclosed; read MSR-hosted copy
reproducibility: Tool later open-sourced; experiment scripts/data not reported; GitLab version not stated
suggested_extensions: Semantic/security oracles; spec inference from traffic or code when no Swagger; back-end log/assertion-based oracles; study coverage vs bug-finding across strategies
evidence_location: Algorithm p.3; limitations p.4 L454-465; Q1 p.5; Tables I-III p.6-8; GitLab bugs p.8-9; production p.9
integrity: Figure 4 values unreadable; tables column-split; no threats section in original
